title: Gabber bound for constructible sheaves on affine opens of an excellent strictly local scheme
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent strictly henselian local scheme of finite Krull dimension $d\geq0$, with $\ell$ invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every constructible sheaf $C$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the ordinary small etale site of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], one has $$H^q(V,C)=0\qquad(q>d),$$ where $q$ is a nonnegative integer and $H^q$ is right-derived global-sections cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Expose XV, Corollary 1.2.2, printed p. 219, applied to the affine open immersion f: V -> X (affine of finite type, X being Noetherian and affine), with the dimension function delta_X(t) = dim of the closure of {t}; then f_*delta_X = delta_X on V (XIV-2.5.2), so f_*delta_X(C) <= dim X = d and 1.2.2 gives H^q(V,C)=0 for q>d. Corollary 1.2.4 (printed p. 220) is the constant-coefficient case Z/n; the route is 1.2.2 directly, not the reduction of 1.2.3.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathbf F_\ell$. First reduce to constructible $B$-module sheaves. For the given $C$ set $C_i=\operatorname{im}(\ell^i:C\to C)$, $0\leq i\leq n$. The kernel/cokernel closure in [thm-constructible-serre] makes each $C_i$ and $Q_i=C_i/C_{i+1}$ constructible. Multiplication by $\ell$ kills $Q_i$, so it is a sheaf of $B$-modules; on each defining locally constant finite stratum, its finite module is simply regarded as a $B$-vector space, hence it remains constructible. We have $C_0=C$, $C_n=0$, and $0\to C_{i+1}\to C_i\to Q_i\to0$. Exact forgetting of module structures is [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Thus these are short exact sequences of abelian sheaves. The cohomology exact sequences in [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder], with the scheme map the identity, show by descending induction on $i$ that vanishing above $d$ for all $Q_i$ implies vanishing above $d$ for $C$.

source.place: XV 1.2.3: reduction to prime coefficients, expanded by the finite multiplication filtration; constructibility: Stacks, etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 09BH, proposition-constructible-over-noetherian (Serre property).

proof.text: On $V$ let $\mathcal A$ be the full class of $B$-module sheaves $F$ with $H^q(V,F)=0$ for every $q>d$, always taking underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology. This class is closed under extensions by the exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] and exact forgetting [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. It is closed under finite sums and retracts: cohomology is additive, so it carries a finite biproduct to the same biproduct, and a split pair to a split pair. Additivity is supplied by the right-derived delta-functor theorem [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]; abelian sheaves have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], and global sections evaluate at the terminal object [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]. Evaluation is additive and preserves kernels: sums of maps and kernels of sheaf morphisms are computed on sections. Thus this is the left exact additive functor to which that theorem applies. The affine open $V$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-per-constructible-finite-open-constant-generation] to $S=V$ and the finite field $B$. It suffices to prove the bound for $\pi_*k_!B_W$, where $\pi:T\to V$ is finite, $T$ is integral, and $k:W\hookrightarrow T$ is a nonempty open immersion. This is the finite-pushforward/trace reduction of XV 1.2.3, in the form proved in XIII 3.7.2; no assertion about arbitrary subquotients of $\mathcal A$ is used.

source.place: XV 1.2.3 and XIII 3.7.2 (printed pp. 219 and 203), expanded using the existing finite-field generator theorem. Its trace input is Stacks Tag 03SH, not an SGA source.

proof.text: Fix one such generator. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R_V$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}E$; $E$ is a domain, finite over $R_V$, by the definition of finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The inclusion $V\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact: an affine open of the affine $X$ is a finite union of principal opens, since principal opens form a basis and $V$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes this inclusion finite type. The map $R_V\to E$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-map-quasi-finite], and the composite $T\to X$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Each of its fibres is either empty or a fibre of the finite map $\pi$, so is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. The criterion [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] now makes $T\to X$ quasi-finite.

source.place: XV 1.2.3; affine Zariski-main preparation. Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01TU, lemma-quasi-compact-open-immersion-finite-presentation (quasi-compact open immersion), 01T3 (finite-type composition), 02NH (finite fibres).

proof.text: The hypothesis of that theorem holds: $R\to E$ is of finite type by Step 3, and by the definition of quasi-finite morphism [pqf-def-quasifinite] every point of the affine $T=\operatorname{Spec}E$ is isolated in its fibre $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$, which is precisely quasi-finiteness of $R\to E$ at every prime [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-ring-map-integral-closure-open], clause (3), to $R\to E$. It gives a finite $R$-subalgebra $A\subseteq E$ for which $T\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open immersion. As a subring of the domain $E$, $A$ is a domain, and this open is dense and nonempty: its generic point maps to the zero prime of $A$. In particular $Y$ is integral and finite over $X$. This uses the subalgebra clause of the cited theorem, rather than assuming an arbitrary finite compactification is integral.

source.place: XV 1.2.3; affine Zariski main theorem, Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00QB, lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure, clause (3).

proof.text: The open $T\subseteq Y$ is exactly $Y\times_XV$. Indeed it is contained in that inverse image by its map to $V$. Put $A_V=A\otimes_R R_V$, the coordinate ring of $Y\times_XV$. The map $A_V\to E$ makes $E$ finite over $A_V$: the same finitely many generators over $R_V$ generate over $A_V$, because the map is compatible with $R_V\to E$. Thus the open immersion $T\to Y\times_XV$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. It is also dense because $T$ is dense in $Y$. Its image is therefore all of $Y\times_XV$, and an open immersion with full image is an isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion]. In particular $T$ is an affine open of $Y$.

source.place: XV 1.2.3, finite-open compactification; the same cartesian identification is written explicitly in Stacks etale-cohomology.tex, proof of lemma-vanishing-easier-coefficients (Tag 0GJH).

proof.text: The finite integral model $Y$ has the required local properties. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], $A$ is a finite product of henselian local rings. Since $A$ is a nonzero domain, only one nonzero factor occurs, so $A$ itself is henselian local and its residue field is finite over the separably closed residue field of $R$. That extension is separably closed by [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-sep-closed]; hence $A$ is strictly henselian. A finite $R$-algebra is finite type, so $A$ is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with multiplicative set $\{1\}$. The subalgebra $A$ is contained in the integral closure of $R$ in $E$, so it is integral over $R$; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-extension-dimension] gives $e=\dim A\leq\dim R=d$. Thus $Y$ is a Noetherian excellent strictly local integral scheme of finite dimension $e\geq0$, with $\ell$ invertible. Excellence implies quasi-excellence by [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: XV 1.2.3 finite-pushforward reduction; Stacks Tags 04GH, 07QU, and the integral-extension dimension theorem.

proof.text: Let $F=T\setminus W$ with its reduced induced closed structure, and let $Z$ be its reduced closure in $Y$, as supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Because $F$ is closed in the open $T$, its closure meets $T$ in precisely $F$; uniqueness of reduced induced structure identifies $F=Z\times_YT$. Thus $F$ is an affine open of $Z$, since it is closed in the affine $T$. The subset $Z$ misses the generic point of the integral $Y$, as the nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ contains that point. Every strict chain in $Z$ can therefore be extended by the generic point of $Y$, proving $\dim Z\leq e-1$ when $Z$ is nonempty. If $e=0$, $Z$ is empty. Otherwise $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ for a proper ideal $I$ in the local $A$. The quotient is strictly henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-quotient], and excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] applied to the finite-type quotient algebra and $\{1\}$. It has the inherited invertible $\ell$.

source.place: XV 1.2.3: remove the closed boundary after finite compactification; XIII 3.7.4 explains this open-closed reduction. Dimension drop is the explicit chain argument, not an additional vanishing theorem.

proof.text: Use the constant-coefficient bound [lem-per-affine-open-strict-local-constant-bound] with $m=\ell$ on the affine open $T\subseteq Y$: $H^q(T,B)=0$ for $q>e$. If $Z$ is nonempty, it is strictly local excellent (therefore quasi-excellent) of dimension $r\leq e-1$, and $F\subseteq Z$ is affine open, so the same bound gives $H^a(F,B)=0$ for $a>r$. In particular, for $q>d$ we have $q>e$ and $q-1\geq d\geq e>r$, hence $H^q(T,B)=H^{q-1}(F,B)=0$. If $Z$ is empty then $F$ is empty and the latter group is zero directly. The proof uses only the constant case of XV 1.2.4, with the actual dimensions $e,r$ of the two finite local models.

source.place: XV Corollaire 1.2.4, printed p. 220, applied twice after the reductions of 1.2.3; XIII 3.7.4 supplies the boundary pattern.

proof.text: Apply the open-closed triangle [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] on $T$ to $B_T[0]$, with closed complement $i:F\hookrightarrow T$ of $k:W\hookrightarrow T$. Constant inverse image is identified with the corresponding constant sheaf by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. As these are exact sheaf functors, degree-zero cohomology of the triangle gives $0\to k_!B_W\to B_T\to i_*B_F\to0$. Forget scalars using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] and take its cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder]. The closed immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] identifies the relevant exact segment as $$H^{q-1}(F,B)\longrightarrow H^q(T,k_!B_W)\longrightarrow H^q(T,B).$$ For $q>d$ both outside groups vanish by Step 8; hence $H^q(T,k_!B_W)=0$. Here $q\geq1$, including $d=0$, so the displayed degrees are nonnegative.

source.place: XV 1.2.3 and XIII 3.7.4: the localization triangle expanded as a short exact sequence; Stacks etale-cohomology.tex Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, and Tag 03QP for finite pushforward.

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] to $\pi:T\to V$ and the underlying abelian sheaf of $k_!B_W$. It gives $$H^q(V,\pi_*k_!B_W)\cong H^q(T,k_!B_W)=0\qquad(q>d).$$ The ordinary module direct image has the same underlying abelian direct image: both evaluate on an etale object $U\to V$ by sections on $U\times_VT$, as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Every generator of Step 2 is consequently in $\mathcal A$. The finite-sum, extension and retract closure established there and [lem-per-constructible-finite-open-constant-generation] put every constructible $B$-module sheaf in $\mathcal A$. Apply this to the $Q_i$ of Step 1 and use its descending induction to obtain the required vanishing for $C$ over $\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. The zero sheaf and empty $V$ give zero cohomology directly and are also allowed by the empty finite constructions.

source.place: XV 1.2.3 (finite pushforward, trace, constant reduction), completed by the finite multiplication filtration of Step 1.
